Guide

What happens on an HGV driving test?

The practical test checks that you can control the vehicle and drive it on the road. The detail is set by DVSA and can be updated, so treat this as an outline and check the official description before test day.

On this page

  1. Vehicle safety questions
  2. Manoeuvres
  3. The road drive
  4. What this site does not claim

Vehicle safety questions

You can be asked to show how you would carry out safety checks on the vehicle, and to explain others. The questions relate to the vehicle you are using for the test.

Manoeuvres

The off-road part looks at control at low speed. For Category C that is the rigid vehicle. For Category C+E it includes the trailer, which is why coupling and reversing with a trailer are practised in training.

  • Category C training
  • Category C+E training

The road drive

The on-road drive looks at how you handle the vehicle in traffic, at junctions and on the kinds of road the test uses. Training routes on a real site reflect the area around that base. No test centre is named on this demonstration.

What this site does not claim

No pass rate is published. A training course prepares you for the test. It does not decide the result. How the test is booked is explained when you enquire.

  • How HGV training works

Related

Courses

  • Category CPractical training for rigid goods vehicles over 3.5 tonnes, for drivers moving up from a car licence.
  • Category C+ETrailer training for drivers who already hold Category C and need the articulated or drawbar entitlement.

Guides

  • How HGV training worksHGV training is a sequence, not a single lesson. You say what you want to drive, the licence you already hold is checked, and the medical, theory and practical steps are planned around that. No duration is stated here.
  • Category C vs Category C+ECategory C and Category C+E are both goods-vehicle entitlements. One is the rigid lorry. The other adds a trailer. They are trained and tested separately.
  • HGV medical explainedA medical is a normal part of getting a lorry licence. This page explains where it sits in the process. It does not say that you will pass, and it does not book an appointment.

Ask about training

If you know which course you need, say so. If you are not sure, say that too.
